title: Handoff Request
description: A durable ask directed at a person. `$id` is a stable identifier, not a fetchable location. Normative meaning is in handoff-protocol-v0.1.md; the wire contract is openapi.yaml.

state.description: `pending` is the only non-terminal state. A server MUST NOT transition out of a terminal state.

version.description: Incremented by every amendment, including a progressive-disclosure step. The receipt records the version the person decided on.

urgency_state.description: Becomes `waiting` when the attempt clock lapses. This MUST NOT affect the request's visibility (I4).

mode.description: Declared per request. A deployment MUST NOT impose `gated` on a class of actions.

expires_at.description: Null means the request never expires. Absence of a TTL is legal and means the ask stands until answered, cancelled, or superseded.

attempt_expires_at.description: The independent attempt clock. On lapse the waiter is nudged exactly once and the request stays pending and listed.

surface_url.description: A locator, not a capability. Opening it MUST prompt for authentication; possession of it is never authority.

receipt.description: Null while pending. At most one decision receipt ever exists for a request (I1).

authorization.description: Minted with the receipt. Single-use, redeemable idempotently per effect_key (I10). Full shape in openapi.yaml#/components/schemas/Authorization.

metadata.description: Opaque to the server. `metadata.hint` is a non-normative analytics label; the core MUST NOT branch on it (I14). Keys prefixed `x-` are stored and returned verbatim and never interpreted.

Duration.description: ISO 8601 duration of exact length, e.g. PT15M, PT4H, P1D, P2W. Years and months are not permitted: P1M is 28 to 31 days depending on when the clock starts, so a TTL or lease expressed in them is not a fixed length. For retention windows see CalendarDuration.

CalendarDuration.description: ISO 8601 duration that may use years and months, resolved against a calendar. Used ONLY for retention windows. It MUST NOT be used for a TTL, an attempt window, a grant expiry, a session lease, or a ladder delay.

WaiterRef.description: Opaque, caller-owned grouping key naming the unit of work that is waiting. A server MUST NOT parse or interpret it.

body.description: Markdown. Rendered to the person and covered by the receipt's rendered digest.

Requires.description: The declaration that drives the renderer, the router, and the validator. There is no request-kind field anywhere in this protocol (I14).

v.description: Envelope version. A server that does not implement the declared version MUST reject with 400 unsupported_requires_version and create nothing (I21).

fields.description: MAY be empty. An empty list means the whole request is an attestation: there is nothing to type and the person acts out of band.

value_sink.description: Where secret values travel. The protocol carries the declaration; the values travel a channel the runtime owns.

ref.description: Opaque provider resource reference. Never a URL.

type.description: Closed and versioned. An unknown type MUST be rejected with 400 unsupported_field_type — never rendered as a text input (I21).

min.description: For `number`, inclusive lower bound. `requires` is digest-covered through `request_digest`, so §1.4 applies: integral in value and within ±(2^53 − 1). A non-integer bound is rejected at raise with 400 invalid_request. JSON Schema's `integer` matches on value, so 2.0 validates here and a Server normalizes it to 2.

max.description: For `number`, inclusive upper bound. Digest-covered on the same terms as `min`.

initial.description: Seed value for `document` and `text` fields. Never used for `secret`.

then.description: A secret field MUST NOT carry a seed value, and its answer carries only {"provided": true} (I7).

CapabilityDeclaration.description: Something the person must be handed in order to be able to answer. Always an opaque handle; the protocol never carries a resolvable address by value (I8).

type.description: Open vocabulary, e.g. `interactive_surface`. An unrecognized type MUST be rejected, never ignored.

provider.description: Registry coordinate. The core MUST NOT match on this string.

resource_ref.description: Opaque provider resource id. Never a URL.

Authority.description: Evaluated at answer time against the answerer's authenticated identity (I6). If any field has type `secret`, the server MUST raise min_role to its administrative role and auth_strength to at least `session`.

auth_strength.description: Ordered link_only < session < reauth < mfa. `link_only` identifies no person and MUST be explicitly enabled by the deployment.

forbid_requester.description: Always true. A requester principal can never answer its own request (I15); the field is present for clarity and a server MUST reject `false`.

reason.description: Shown to the person: why this level of authority is being asked for.

Target.description: Resolved to a set of principals through one resolution port. The core MUST NOT branch per kind.

Routing.description: Deployment policy, resolved server-side at raise time and snapshotted onto the request so a later policy edit cannot change what happened.

LadderRung.description: A rung mints deliveries, never a request (I3).

TtlPolicy.description: Fail toward a typed terminal answer, never toward silence; when the answer must be guessed, guess no.

default_answer.description: REQUIRED when on_expiry is `default`, and MUST have been declared at raise time. The resulting receipt records actor.type = "policy".
